subject.title: ci: harden HTTP and local-auth gates against transient failures

question: Should the team first make runner capacity and local-Convex saturation observable in CI, then land separately scoped HTTP-fixture and local-auth query/retry hardening, or treat the current retries as sufficient?
rationale: The report crosses hosted-runner provisioning, CI failure policy, and application subscription behavior; source history establishes adjacent owners but does not establish which boundary maintainers want to own or change first.

options.title: Diagnose then split fixes
options.body: Add bounded capacity and saturation diagnostics first, then land independent fixes for the retryable GitHub lookup and the local-auth read/retry path.

options.title: Accept current retry behavior
options.body: Keep the existing gate design and only rerun intermittent failures, accepting that the reported infrastructure signal remains indirect.

recommendation.title: Diagnose then split fixes
recommendation.body: Add bounded capacity and saturation diagnostics first, then land independent fixes for the retryable GitHub lookup and the local-auth read/retry path.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns the local-auth CI setup boundary most directly.
